learning_outcomes.text: Provide the student with basic knowledge of programming procedures for mathematical calculation, for computer-aided design applied to engineering projects and studies, as well as the standardized representation of elements and equipment.
Introduce the student to the use of computer applications used in engineering for drawing representation.

syllabus_topics: Practical application of Matlab in engineering
Introduction to CAD systems. Principles of Standardization
Normalized projection methods: European system and American system. Normalized views
Justification of the CAD program used
Define the limits of a drawing
Save current drawing with another name
Utilities in precision drawing and designation modes. Commands II. Standardized applications I
Selection of point type and scale
Aids for precision drawing. Commands III. Standardized applications II
Drawing and editing texts. Standardized applications IV
Editing justification of multiple texts at once
Drawing and editing commands for objects with self-thickness. Standardized applications V
Obtaining component objects from a composite object
Layer control and object properties. Standardized applications VI
Partial deletion and fragmentation of objects
Marking an object with a determined number of divisions
Marking an object in divisions of the same length
Freehand drawing and hatching. Standardized applications IX
Blocks and attributes. Standardized applications X
Application to threaded elements and gears
Dimensioning systems. Types of dimensions. Dimensioning elements
Dimensioning editor compatible with previous versions
Dimensioning of conical and pyramidal elements
Replacing variable values in associative dimensions

assessment_methods.method: Continuous Assessment of Standardization (from seminar work)
Standardization Final Exam (theoretical and practical tests)
Continuous Assessment of CAD (from seminar work)

assessment_rules: The final grade is the arithmetic mean of three equally weighted parts: Matlab, Standardization, and CAD. A passing grade in each part is mandatory to pass the course; otherwise, the maximum final grade is 4.00. Students choose between two evaluation options: Option 1 (Continuous and Final Evaluation) weights continuous assessments for 30-40% of each part and final exams for 60-70%, with approved part grades saved for subsequent calls. Option 2 (Global Evaluation) relies on final and extra exams for each part, with no approved part grades saved, and may include specific minimum scores for sub-tests.
